questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=t-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(t-1)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,({t}^{2}-2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-{t}^{2}+t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-1+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{t-1}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})} \\  & =\sqrt{3}(t-1)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,2]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=t+{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(t+{t}^{2})^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}+{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}+\frac{{t}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}+8+\frac{32}{5} \\  & =\frac{256}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{256}{15}}=\frac{16}{\sqrt{15}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=2t-{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=2t-{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=1,\,p(0)=0,\,p(-1)=-3.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(0)p(0)+p(-1)p(-1)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(0)]^{2}+[p(-1)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+0+9} \\  & =\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(-2)y(-2)+x(0)y(0)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=3-t+{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=3-t+{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(-2)=9,\,p(0)=3,\,p(2)=5.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(-2)p(-2)+p(0)p(0)+p(2)p(2)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(-2)]^{2}+[p(0)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(9)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81+9+25} \\  & =\sqrt{115}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =1\cdot 1+3\cdot (2\cdot 2)+2\cdot (3\cdot 3) \\  & =1+12+18 \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{31}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{31}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{31}}{31}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
